newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen officials to promote B shares overseas.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen officials to promote B shares overseas.

text.p: Shenzhen securities authorities and officials from major listed firms in the city bordering Hong Kong headed for Asia and Europe on Thursday to promote their hard currency B shares, the Securities Times said.

The delegation, headed by Liu Xinhua, who is director of Shenzhen Securities Management Office, comprised officials from 10 large Shenzhen-listed B share firms and several domestic brokerages, the Shenzhen-based newspaper said on Friday.

They would recommend good B share firms to overseas investment banks and fund managers and introduce foreigners to the existing environment and outlook of Shenzhen Special Economic Zone and its securities market, it said.
The delegation would stop in Hong Kong, Singapore, South Korea, the United States and European countries including Britain and the Netherlands, it said.

The listed companies represented in the delegation included China International Marine Containers Co Ltd, property developer China Vanke Co Ltd, Guangdong Electric Power Development Co Ltd and diesel engine maker Changchai Co Ltd, it said.

Analysts said Shenzhen's B share market, like its Shanghai counterpart, has been plagued by problems such as falling earnings and the poor transparency of listed companies, as well as stagnant liquidity because of the limited size of the market.
B shares in Shenzhen are quoted in Hong Kong dollars, with those in Shanghai in U.S. dollars.
